disposition_reason: Farm survey of 70 Peruvian cacao plantations (Feb-Apr 2014) reporting regional and genotype mean Cd, Cr, Ni and Pb (plus non-tracked elements) in dried cacao beans and leaves by AAS. Only the min/max regional and genotype means are printed in text; the remaining means are shown in bar charts (Fig. 2, Fig. 3) and were read from the figures.
disposition_locator: Section 3.1 and Fig. 2 (p.795); Section 3.2 and Fig. 3 (p.795-796); Section 3.3 (p.796-797)

study.material_scope: cacao beans extracted from sampled fruits (composite per plantation), oven-dried at 60 C and milled; leaves as context
study.growing_origin_vs_market: grown in Peru: Tumbes, Piura, Cajamarca, Amazonas (North); San Martin, Huanuco, Junin (Center per Table 1/methods; abstract places Junin in South); Cuzco (South)
study.sampling_unit: plantation (3 random plots x 10 trees; fruits pooled into a composite bean sample); Table 2 correlation uses n = 72
study.method: 500 mg dried sample digested in 10 ml HNO3 (65%)/HClO4 (98%) 4:1, block 120 C 3 h then 200 C 2 h; flame AAS (Varian Spectra 55B); triplicate determinations averaged
study.lod_loq: not reported (Cr in two genotypes stated 'below the limit of detection' without a value)
study.basis: dry weight (beans oven-dried at 60 C and milled; fermentation/shelling not described)
study.qa: three repetitions per sample; no CRM, recovery or blank data reported

controls.outcome: Bean Cd means ranged 0.15 ± 0.8 ug/g (Native from Satipo) to 1.8 ± 0.4 ug/g (Spontaneous Hybrids) (P <= 0.05 among genotypes, Table S2); Fig. 3 shows CCN51/ICS95/ICS39 about 0.5 ug/g vs CCN51/ICS95 about 1.0 and CCN51 about 0.9 ug/g. Authors: Blanco Piurano, CCN51, CCN51/ICS95 and spontaneous hybrids exceeded 0.80 ug/g; CCN51/ICS95/ICS39 'could lead to low Cd'. Genotype is confounded with region and soil; not a controlled comparison.

controls.control: Leaf Cd as a predictor of bean Cd (monitoring)
controls.comparator: Correlation between leaf and bean element concentrations (n = 72)
controls.outcome: Bean Cd correlated with leaf Cd r = 0.74 and with leaf Zn r = 0.21 (P <= 0.05); bean Ni with leaf Ni r = 0.68; bean Pb vs leaf Pb r = 0.12 (not significant). Leaf Cd regional means 0.23 ± 0.62 (Cuzco) to 2.50 ± 0.62 ug/g (Tumbes).

controls.control: Regional sourcing (avoid Amazonas, Piura, Tumbes for low-Cd lots)
controls.outcome: Tumbes 1.78 ± 0.35 ug/g and Cuzco 0.17 ± 0.41 ug/g (printed); figure-read Piura ~1.55, Amazonas ~0.96, San Martin ~0.80, Cajamarca ~0.78, Huanuco ~0.65, Junin ~0.43 ug/g. Regional differences in bean Cd were not statistically significant (P > 0.05, Table S1).

regulatory.instrument: Commission Regulation (EU) No 488/2014 amending Reg. 1881/2006 (as cited)
regulatory.product: chocolate containing >=50% of cacao bean solids (source wording); used by the authors as a 'critical value' for beans

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Summary lists San Martin bean Cd 1.00 ± 0.87 ug/g; in the primary 1.00 ± 0.87 is San Martin bean Cr. San Martin bean Cd is not printed (Fig. 2 ~0.8).
Summary gives bean Pb maximum 3.00 ± 1.39 ug/g (Piura); primary: 3.78 ± 0.39 ug/g in Piura.
Summary gives bean Ni minimum 3.5 ± 2.1; primary: 3.5 ± 2.00 ug/g (Tumbes).
Summary leaf Cd values 'Tumbes 1.00 ± 0.87; Amazonas 2.86 ± 0.31' are wrong: leaf Cd was 2.50 ± 0.62 in Tumbes (maximum); 2.86 ± 0.31 is leaf Cr in Amazonas; 1.00 ± 0.87 is bean Cr in San Martin.
Summary says Native from Maranon had the lowest bean Cd (0.10 ± 0.9); 0.10 ± 0.9 is the leaf Cd of Native from Maranon; lowest bean Cd was Native from Satipo 0.15 ± 0.8 ug/g.
Summary says 'more than 57%' of beans exceeded 0.8 ug/g; primary text says 'nearly 57%' (and highlights contradict with '>60% below').
Summary places Junin in the South with Cuzco; methods/Table 1 place Junin in the Center (abstract says South: internally inconsistent).
Summary says 'Short growing season sampled (dry season only)'; primary only gives February-April 2014 and does not characterise season.
Summary implies soil Cd/Zn data are in this paper's results via correlations; soil data are reported in Arevalo-Gardini et al. 2016 and only used in the cluster analysis here.
unresolved: Most regional and genotype means (all except the printed min/max) are figure readings with about ±0.1 ug/g uncertainty; Supplementary Tables S1/S2 with exact values were not available.
n per region and per genotype not reported; whether the regional ± is SD or SE not stated.
LOD/LOQ not reported for any element; no CRM/recovery; flame AAS at sub-1 ug/g Cd and ~1 ug/g Pb is near typical flame AAS limits, so low values may be imprecise.
Bean processing state (fermented or not, shelled or whole) not stated; beans were extracted from fruits and oven-dried, implying unfermented whole beans.
Inconsistent statements on share exceeding 0.8 ug/g (nearly 57% exceed vs >60% below).
Cr bars absent for Junin and Cuzco in Fig. 2 though text gives San Martin 1.00 as the minimum.
